This is a present-day livestock guardian portrait, not a reconstruction of an ancient dog. Use the supplied photograph only for the adult dog's morphology and coat: heavy developed broad head, substantial slightly longer-than-tall trunk, strong coherent limbs, natural triangular drop ears, broad muzzle with some grey-white hair, dense straight medium black coat with restrained white chest and foot markings, and complete natural tail with longer underside fur and a small pale terminal tuft. Do not turn it into a juvenile, a curly-coated dog or a short-faced mastiff.

Native output must be 1536×1024 landscape. Show one adult dog standing in a newly composed dog-eye-level three-quarter pose, head gently turned toward the viewer, with a calm attentive expression. All four coherent legs and paws must be visibly grounded on firm open earth. Keep credible shoulder, elbow, hock and paw connections, natural fur and subtle contact shadows. Show the entire attached natural tail continuously from its base through its tapered free end, carried low in a gentle curve, separate from the hind legs. Keep clear contrast around the dark tail and pale endpoint. Preserve generous space around the full head, ears, body, feet and tail; no cropped extremities.

Place the dog beside a quiet pasture opening in the Epirus mountain foothills in late spring, with sparse short grass, firm earth under every paw, low rocks at a distance and restrained cool-green hills in soft daylight. This setting interprets the documented contemporary mountain flock-guardian role. Compose a new standing pose, setting and lighting; do not copy the indoor show scene, people, shoe overlap, collar or leash. No people, other animals, ancient architecture, reconstruction imagery, gear, text, logos, watermark, plastic fur, invented limbs or malformed paws.
images.scene: Quiet pasture opening in the Epirus mountain foothills in late spring, sparse short grass, firm earth, distant low rocks, cool-green hills and soft daylight.
